title: Κύνες δύο
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 175. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔχων τις δύο κύνας, τὸν μὲν θηρεύειν ἐδίδασκε, τὸν δὲ οἰκουρὸν ἐποίησε.
sentences.tr: Echōn tis dyo kynas, ton men thēreuein edidaske, ton de oikouron epoiēse.
sentences.l: A man having two dogs was teaching the one to hunt, and made the other a house-keeper.
sentences.i: A man who had two dogs trained the one to hunt and made the other a watchdog.
sentences.n: μέν … δέ divides the pair. διδάσκω takes the accusative of the pupil and an infinitive of what he is taught. οἰκουρός is the one who keeps the house, and it stands as a predicate accusative after ἐποίησε: he made him a guard.

sentences.t: Καὶ δή, εἴ ποτε ὁ θηρευτὴς ἐξιὼν ἐπ’ ἄγραν συνελάμβανέ τι, ἐκ τούτου μέρος καὶ τῷ ἑτέρῳ παρέβαλλεν.
sentences.tr: Kai dē, ei pote ho thēreutēs exiōn ep’ agran synelambane ti, ek toutou meros kai tōi heterōi pareballen.
sentences.l: And so, whenever the hunting one, going out after game, took anything, from it the master would throw a share to the other one as well.
sentences.i: And so whenever the hunting dog went out after game and took something, the master would throw a share of it to the other dog as well.
sentences.n: εἴ ποτε with the imperfect indicative is the past general condition, "whenever". παραβάλλω is the ordinary word for throwing food down in front of an animal. The subject of παρέβαλλεν is left unexpressed and is the master, not the hunting dog — the point of the quarrel that follows.

sentences.t: Ἀγανακτοῦντος δὲ τοῦ θηρευτικοῦ καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ὀνειδίζοντος, εἴ γε αὐτὸς μὲν ἐξιὼν παρ’ ἕκαστα μοχθεῖ, ὁ δὲ οὐδὲν ποιῶν τοῖς αὐτοῦ πόνοις ἐντρυφᾷ, ἐκεῖνος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτόν· « Ἀλλὰ μὴ ἐμὲ μέμφου, ἀλλὰ τὸν δεσπότην, ὃς οὐ πονεῖν με ἐδίδαξεν, ἀλλοτρίους δὲ πόνους κατεσθίειν. »
sentences.tr: Aganaktountos de tou thēreutikou kai ton heteron oneidizontos, ei ge autos men exiōn par’ hekasta mochthei, ho de ouden poiōn tois autou ponois entryphāi, ekeinos ephē pros auton· « Alla mē eme memphou, alla ton despotēn, hos ou ponein me edidaxen, allotrious de ponous katesthiein. »
sentences.l: But the hunting dog being indignant and reproaching the other — seeing that he himself, going out, toils at every turn, while the other, doing nothing, lives softly on his labours — that one said to him: « Do not blame me, but the master, who taught me not to toil, but to eat up the labours of others. »
sentences.i: The hunting dog grew indignant and reproached the other: he himself went out and toiled at every turn, while the other did nothing and lived softly on his labours. And the other said to him: « Do not blame me, but the master, who taught me not to work but to eat up what others have worked for. »
sentences.n: A genitive absolute (ἀγανακτοῦντος … ὀνειδίζοντος) carries the whole complaint before the main verb ἔφη arrives. εἴ γε here gives the ground of the reproach, "seeing that". παρ’ ἕκαστα is "at every turn"; ἐντρυφάω with the dative is to live in luxury on a thing. In the reply the one verb ἐδίδαξεν is split between two infinitives by οὐ … δέ.

sentences.t: Οὕτω καὶ τῶν παίδων οἱ ῥᾴθυμοι οὐ μεμπτέοι εἰσίν, ὅταν αὐτοὺς οἱ γονεῖς οὕτως ἄγωσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtō kai tōn paidōn hoi rhāithymoi ou mempteoi eisin, hotan autous hoi goneis houtōs agōsin.
sentences.l: So too among children the idle are not to be blamed, when their parents bring them up so.
sentences.n: μεμπτέος is a verbal adjective in -τέος, which states what must or must not be done: "not to be blamed". ὅταν with the subjunctive ἄγωσιν is the general temporal clause, of what holds in any such case. ἄγω is used of leading a child along, so of rearing and training.
